findings.title: Tiny Markdown table metadata can trigger unbounded cell allocation
findings.summary: A caller-controlled cells paragraph range is converted into an unbounded count and used to append padding cells. A tiny Markdown table with a range such as p0-p1000000000 causes roughly a billion padding entries to be allocated before DOCX assembly, exhausting CPU and memory in Rust, Python, or WASM conversion hosts.

severity.rationale: A small untrusted Markdown input can exhaust or terminate its processing host. Reachability is direct through public byte/string APIs; remote or multi-user service exposure is conditional, and there is no confidentiality or integrity compromise.
severity.changeConditions: Process memory/CPU limits and worker isolation constrain impact; a shared remotely exposed conversion service would increase operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Static source tracing establishes the unchecked numeric count, default public conversion path, and count-driven Vec growth; runtime exhaustion was deliberately not executed.

codeEvidence.label: Table cell range has no amplification bound
codeEvidence.explanation: Checked arithmetic prevents overflow but accepts arbitrarily large representable cell counts.

codeEvidence.label: Declared count directly drives vector growth
codeEvidence.explanation: For a table row without break markers, padding grows until the attacker-selected n; actual Markdown cells do not bound it.

codeEvidence.label: Public conversion calls parser before output assembly
codeEvidence.explanation: Normal valid conversion options reach read(), whose line 155 computes table_plans before event-level view filtering.

codeEvidence.label: Sibling paragraph range already has an explicit limit
codeEvidence.explanation: MOST_EMPTY exists but is not applied to row_paragraphs.

rootCause.summary: Table metadata range parsing omits the existing per-range bound and the table planner trusts the resulting count for allocation.

findings.remediation: Validate row_paragraphs with the same bounded range helper used elsewhere, impose a total table/output cell budget before allocation, and return a structured refusal rather than silently processing an oversized range.

counterEvidence: checked_sub and checked_add reject descending/overflowing ranges but do not limit large valid ranges.
The count branch requires one metadata range per actual table row and no break marker; a single-header-row table can satisfy both.
Sibling paragraph_range caps MOST_EMPTY at 100000, but this branch does not call it.
SECURITY.md recommends process limits; these limit blast radius without preventing the input amplification.
limitations: No application code or resource-exhaustion proof was executed.
Actual remote/shared service deployment is not established.
validation.summary: Independently traced metadata collection in table_plans, checked range parsing, the no-break row branch, and Rust/Python/WASM public conversion callers. No range or output budget intervenes before padding allocation.

dataflow.summary: markdown_to_docx(markdown) -> read -> table_plans -> view_notes::table_line -> row_paragraphs count -> plan_table -> pad.push until n.

likelihood.summary: Deterministic input amplification; attacker access to a shared conversion host is deployment-dependent.

reachability.summary: Rust markdown_to_docx and Python/WASM wrappers accept caller-controlled text; ordinary valid options reach the table planner without admitting a DOCX archive first.
reachability.attacker: Document supplier to an application that converts untrusted Markdown
preconditions: Metadata contains one range per table row, with a large valid range and no paragraph break in the affected row.

attackPath.summary: Untrusted Markdown range metadata crosses into unchecked output cardinality.

remediationTests: With a tiny one-row table, a range exceeding the configured table budget must fail promptly without allocating proportional output.
Cover valid ranges at the inclusive limit, descending/overflow ranges, multiple rows, and ranges with and without break markers across the shared public API.

findings.title: Unbounded document table spans exhaust memory during rendering
findings.summary: Untrusted DOCX table gridSpan and HTML/MHT altChunk colspan values become unrestricted output column counts. A tiny document can request a billion columns, causing layout-vector allocation or generated XML expansion before any output budget, exhausting memory and CPU despite package admission.

severity.rationale: Public render/convert APIs accept untrusted documents and a tiny accepted input produces arbitrarily large generated XML. Impact is availability of the processing host; remote/shared exposure depends on the embedding application.
severity.changeConditions: Memory/CPU-limited isolated workers constrain impact; shared conversion service exposure increases affected availability.

confidence.rationale: Source establishes package admission followed by HTML expansion, unrestricted colspan parsing, and direct count-driven XML generation; no destructive runtime proof was run.

codeEvidence.label: Colspan has no upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: A small HTML attribute can select any positive representable span.

codeEvidence.label: One output element per declared column
codeEvidence.code:
let cols = table
            .rows
            .iter()
            .map(|r| r.iter().map(|c| c.span).sum::<usize>())
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(1)
            .max(1);
        let col_w = 9360 / cols;
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker-controlled spans become output column count.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded XML expansion loop
codeEvidence.explanation: Even a single cell can cause billions of grid elements to be allocated.

codeEvidence.label: Rendering expands relationship-selected HTML
codeEvidence.explanation: Input admission precedes expansion, so its inflated input-byte budgets do not bound generated XML.

codeEvidence.label: OOXML span accepts huge positive values
codeEvidence.explanation: Raw DOCX tables can reach the same unrestricted numeric cardinality without an altChunk.

codeEvidence.label: Span totals directly size layout vectors
codeEvidence.explanation: A tiny gridSpan value represented by a short decimal string can trigger gigabytes of column allocation.

codeEvidence.label: Merge bookkeeping also grows with span
codeEvidence.explanation: The unbounded count also propagates into merge-state allocation and iteration.

rootCause.summary: DOCX gridSpan and imported HTML colspan are trusted as output column cardinalities with only a lower bound. Both document-table paths lack a shared grid/output budget before generation and allocation.

findings.remediation: Enforce a common total table/grid budget for direct OOXML spans and HTML/MHT import before output generation or vector allocation. Reject excessive spans and use checked cumulative totals, returning a typed conversion refusal.

counterEvidence: Archive inflation and XML input limits apply to original package bytes, which can remain tiny.
The parser defaults invalid/zero spans to one but valid huge positive spans remain unrestricted.
Process resource limits recommended by SECURITY.md constrain host impact without rejecting the expansion.
limitations: No resource-exhaustion execution or observed service deployment.
validation.summary: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing. Independently verified direct OOXML gridSpan parsing (14211-14215), column occupancy allocation (13601-13615), and merge vector resize (14637-14642); they share the missing bounded table cardinality control.

dataflow.summary: DOCX main document w:altChunk r:id -> relationship target part -> chunk_html -> html_to_wml -> Builder::start(td,colspan) -> end_table cols -> XML output loop. Ordinary OOXML path: w:gridSpan/@w:val -> cell_span -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> cols allocation -> merge-state resize.

impact.summary: Processing-host memory exhaustion or prolonged CPU use.

likelihood.summary: The expansion is deterministic; exposure to untrusted callers depends on the embedding host.

reachability.summary: Public docx_to_png, render, report and PDF/layout paths call with_layout; attacker only needs to supply package bytes accepted by existing admission.
preconditions: A host renders/converts an attacker-controlled DOCX containing either a large w:gridSpan or an internal HTML/MHT chunk with a large colspan.

remediationTests: A tiny altChunk with colspan 1000000000 must fail before large output allocation.
Cover inclusive limits, cumulative spans across cells, integer overflow, nested tables, and both HTML and MHT import.
Cover direct OOXML gridSpan with tiny/no initial tblGrid, gridBefore/gridAfter variants, and merge bookkeeping as well as imported colspan.

surfaces.label: Markdown table metadata admission
surfaces.notes: Validated unbounded row range -> padding allocation; src/markdown/view_notes.rs:1011-1022 and src/markdown/write.rs:1265-1269. Existing MOST_EMPTY cap applies only to sibling parser.

surfaces.label: Legacy DOC overlapping text-piece amplification
surfaces.notes: Independent inspection rejects this candidate: pieces() derives adjacent CP boundaries from the same array (src/legacy_doc.rs:1092-1094), and main_text rejects any decreasing adjacent CP pair (1154-1155). This prevents the proposed repeated overlapping ranges even though coverage validation stops at the story boundary.

candidate.originalMessage: legacy_doc::main_text validates contiguous pieces only until `covered >= ccp_text` (lines1161-1175) but second pass iterates all pieces with cp_start<ccp_text (1181-1229). Repeated overlapping pieces after the first complete piece duplicate the same story bytes N times, enabling O(file_size²) memory/CPU expansion.

surfaces.label: DOCX and HTML/MHT table-span cardinality
surfaces.notes: Validated direct gridSpan allocation (src/convert/mod.rs:14211-14215,13601-13615,14637-14642) and imported colspan expansion (src/convert/altchunk.rs:562-567,469-491), consolidated under missing document-table cardinality control.

candidate.originalMessage: admission::check_xml_depth ignores Event::DocType (admission.rs:788-823), while parse_document skips a DOCTYPE only through the first literal '>' (xmllinq/parse.rs:539-543). A legal DTD internal-subset comment can contain `<!-->` followed by thousands of `<a>` strings, then `-->]>` and the ordinary document root. Admission sees one DocType and shallow real root; custom parser exits the DTD at the comment's first '>', recursively parses hidden `<a>` strings through parse_element:663-665, bypassing max_xml_depth and overflowing the call stack. WmlDocument::from_bytes -> main_document is direct admitted-byte path (wml_document.rs:52-58,85-95); strict validate_xml would reject DTD, but that path does not invoke it.
